answer: Sybil resistance arises when trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: honest mass mixes across well-connected regions, while a sybil cluster is separated by a sparse external cut. Its low conductance limits escape probability at each step, so min-cut transitivity bounds its stationary mass and aggregate voting weight, even if internally dense. A trellis of attestations may expose the ridge, while honest anchors remain an oasis.
